newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen gaining on baht, politics.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen gaining on baht, politics.

text.p: Thai stocks are expected to rebound on Friday as the baht is stable in foreign exchange markets and Finance Minsister Amnuay Viravan looks certain to stay in his job, analysts said.
The SET Index finished 13.43 points lower on Wednesday to a new eight-year low of 557.87. The SET 50 is at 40.40.

"I expect a short term technical rebound due mainly to the stronger baht and the Prime Minister's confirmation that Amnuay will stay in the cabinet," said Chinda Petchployngamet, head of research at Thai Rung Reung.
Locals are likely to be the primary buyers, and are expected to outweigh continuing sales by foreign investors who are still concerned about the outlook for the currency, traders said.
A rash of morning corporate results are likely to have a minimal a market heavily dominated by currency, economic and political concerns, traders said.
"The results so far suggest that GDP growth this year is unlikely to reach six percent. If there is any effect from this morning's results I would expect it to be very short term," Chinda said.
